sections.h2: How a McHenry homeowner goes about selling
sections.html:
Three paths are open. An agent can list the house, you can find a buyer yourself, or you can deal with a purchaser who accepts the house as it sits and brings no lender. Once a contract exists, every path ends at the same county filing: a transfer declaration plus a recorded deed.

Condition and calendar settle the choice. Patience plus a tidy interior favors open houses. Worn systems, a tenant, an estate in limbo or a hard closing date tilt toward a direct purchase.

What follows sticks to McHenry itself: housing figures, the permit rules at 333 S Green Street, how city water accounts change hands, and what the county recorder expects.

The city is in east-central McHenry County, about 55 miles from the Chicago Loop and 35 from O'Hare, over about 13 square miles of land, and is organized around two state routes, 31 and 120. By the 1920s the Fox River and nearby lakes had made the town a summer destination, and summer cottages spread along the river. Subdivisions were annexed on every side from the late 1940s onward, such as Boone Creek, Glacier Ridge, Legend Lakes, Liberty Trails and Prairie Lakes.

Population was 27,135 in 2020 and is estimated at 29,217 for mid-2025, up 6.8 percent. Owners live in 74.4 percent of the 11,897 households. A typical owned home is valued at $266,500, median rent runs $1,553, and household income sits at $86,315 (all figures 2020 to 2024). Roughly three in four homes are owner-occupied, so the people you compete with are mostly neighbors. Getting to work takes 29.0 minutes on average.

McHenry Community High School District 156 and McHenry School District 15 (five elementary and three middle schools) both serve the city.

  • Roads: Route 31 and Route 120 cross in the middle of town and carry most traffic in and out.
  • Rail: the city is the last stop on a Metra branch that offers weekday trains into downtown Chicago.
  • Trails and parks: the Prairie Trail runs through the center, while Moraine Hills State Park, anchored by 48-acre Lake Defiance, lies on the east side.
  • Airports: O'Hare and Milwaukee Mitchell are the closest public international airports.

Downtown is split into Green Street, Riverside Drive and Main Street, tied together by a 0.73 mile Riverwalk along Boone Creek and the Fox River.

Expect scrutiny of the roof, gutters, attic insulation, furnace and basement. The area sees about 34.5 inches of snow a year, and yearly precipitation totals close to 37 inches, peaking in May and June, so a basement that smells damp or a sump pump that cycles constantly will show up on an inspection.

Glacial lakes, Boone Creek and the Fox River give the area its character and also its drainage questions. If the lot lies near the water, find out its flood zone designation before you name a price.

sections.h2: Permits when a McHenry house is on the market
sections.html:
Most remodeling and home improvement jobs in McHenry need a building permit. Sort out any open or missing permits early. The Community Development Department answers at 815-363-2170 and sits in the Municipal Center, 333 S Green Street.

Most residential permit applications are processed within 10 business days, and the clock does not start until everything needed for review has been submitted. Some permits are issued faster:

  • Reroof, siding, and windows or doors.
  • Water heater and furnace or air conditioner replacement.
  • Sewer or water repair.

Those counter-based permits come back immediately for walk-in applicants and within a day for online ones. The permit fee already covers the inspections, which need a day's notice and are booked in three-hour windows (9 to noon or 1 to 4, except roofing and siding, which run 10 to 2). Same-day inspections are not offered.

If an earlier owner skipped paperwork on a deck or basement, the department can say what finishing it involves. Investors often absorb that cost; buyers with mortgages tend to raise it.

sections.h2: Where a McHenry deed goes after closing
sections.html:
The county Recorder's Office handles it, not city hall. A document that meets state formatting rules and comes with the right payment is recorded the same day, then mailed back in roughly two working days. For fees, ring 815-334-4110.

Sale prices are visible through a PTAX-203 or MyDec form that can accompany the deed. The state levy is set in 35 ILCS 200/31-15 at fifty cents for every $500 of value, with revenue stamps as proof. No McHenry County municipality adds its own transfer tax. For ownership by parcel number, the Assessor's number is 815-334-4290; for tax bills, the County Treasurer's is 815-334-4072.

sections.h2: What a McHenry seller owes the buyer and the city utility
sections.html:
Under 765 ILCS 77/20 the seller fills out every item of the statutory report and puts it in the buyer's hands before anyone signs a contract. Finish it while offers are still coming in.

City water and sewer bills arrive every two months, and accounts fall on even or odd billing months depending on the account number prefix. McHenry publishes a Water/Sewer Transfer Form that records the ownership date along with billing addresses for the outgoing and incoming owner. Submitting it fixes the date your final bill stops.

The title company will ask for a loan payoff figure if you owe on the house, along with the parcel number and your latest tax bill. Put the transfer form, the disclosure report, the permit history and those papers in one folder, so a buyer or title officer gets answers in a single request. Call the County Treasurer at 815-334-4072 if you are unsure whether a tax bill is paid.

sections.h2: Which McHenry selling route fits which situation?
sections.html:
Set the three paths side by side before choosing.

  • Agent listing: the largest audience, in return for showings, an appraisal and inspection, and possible repair requests from the buyer.
  • Owner-handled sale: control over price and timing, with the paperwork and promotion landing on you.
  • Direct sale for cash: quicker, with fewer conditions, and priced around the repairs ahead.

With any offer, insist on a written copy and read each closing cost line.

faqs.q: Do roof and water heater swaps in McHenry need city sign-off?
faqs.a: Yes. Both jobs sit on the city's counter-based permit list, which means same-visit approval in person or a one-day turnaround online. Community Development at 815-363-2170 can say what your project requires.

faqs.q: Is there a McHenry city transfer stamp?
faqs.a: No. None of the county's municipalities levy their own, so the state's fifty cents on each $500 (35 ILCS 200/31-15) is the charge.
The McHenry County Recorder, at 815-334-4110. Documents that conform and carry the right payment are recorded the day they arrive.

faqs.q: How does the city water account change hands?
faqs.a: McHenry bills every second month and provides a Water/Sewer Transfer Form noting the ownership date. File it at closing and each owner pays only for their own period.

faqs.q: Will anyone buy a McHenry house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. Illinois asks only that the disclosure report precede the contract; fixes are bargained over afterward. Mortgage-backed buyers lean on repair requests, while investors price the work into their offer.
